# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 56 (Bu-Vb Pc56)

**ID:** Bu-Vb Pc56  
**Section:** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (bu-vb)  
**Collection:** Vinaya  
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 56  
**Title (English, from literature):** Lighting a fire  
**tipitaka.org (CST):** [https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul0.xml](https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul0.xml)

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 56 (titled *Jotika*) governs the lighting of fires by Buddhist monastics. The rule establishes that a monk who kindles a fire to warm himself commits an offense that must be confessed (*pācittiya*), unless he is ill [Dhammika, Broken Buddha; Horner, Cullavagga]. In the rule's origin story, several monks built a fire on a cold winter night using an old hollow log; when a cobra nestled inside sprang out and frightened them, the Buddha promulgated the prohibition [Dhammika, Broken Buddha].

 Parallels survive in Chinese, Sanskrit, and Tibetan recensions representing the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Dharmaguptaka, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsāṅghika, Lokottaravāda, and Kāśyapīya lineages, as well as the *Upāliparipṛcchā*. An English translation has been prepared by Bhikkhu Brahmali.
